questions.scenario: Module `ng.itlearning.fx` has a public class `ng.itlearning.fx.internal.Cache`. Another module requires `ng.itlearning.fx` but fails to compile when it uses `Cache`.
questions.question: Why?
options: The class needs a public constructor
Only exported packages are accessible to other modules; ng.itlearning.fx.internal isn't exported
questions.explanation: Strong encapsulation: public is not enough across modules. The package must be exported, possibly only to specific modules.

questions.scenario: Jackson throws InaccessibleObjectException when deserialising into DTOs in package `ng.itlearning.fx.dto`, which is exported.
questions.question: What does the module need?
options: opens ng.itlearning.fx.dto (ideally only to the Jackson module, tools.jackson.databind in Jackson 3) to allow deep reflection
questions.explanation: exports allows access to public members only; reflective access to private fields needs opens.

questions.scenario: A consumer module should discover any number of RateProvider implementations at runtime without referencing their classes.
questions.question: Which pair of directives and API achieves this?
options: uses RateProvider in the consumer, provides RateProvider with Impl in each provider, and ServiceLoader.load(RateProvider.class)
questions.explanation: The service loader mechanism decouples consumers from providers; adding a provider module adds an implementation without recompiling the consumer.

questions.scenario: During migration, a plain (non-modular) library jar is placed on the module path next to your named application module.
questions.question: How is the library treated?
options: As an automatic module: named from Automatic-Module-Name or the file name, reading all modules and exporting all its packages
questions.explanation: Automatic modules bridge the classpath world and named modules during top-down migration. Jars on the classpath form the unnamed module instead.

questions.scenario: The security team wants smaller container images with fewer JDK components for a Spring Boot service.
questions.question: Which tools produce a trimmed runtime?
options: jdeps to find the required modules, then jlink to build a runtime image containing only those modules
questions.explanation: jdeps --print-module-deps lists what the application uses; jlink assembles a custom runtime with just those modules.

questions.scenario: A module's public API returns types from module `ng.itlearning.money`. Every consumer has to add `requires ng.itlearning.money` themselves.
questions.question: How can the API module spare its consumers that step?
questions.explanation: requires transitive grants implied readability: anyone who requires the API module can also read the money module.

questions.scenario: On a Java 25 JDK, a file `Hello.java` contains only `void main() { IO.println("hi"); }`.
questions.question: What happens with `java Hello.java`?
options: It runs and prints hi: compact source files and instance main methods are standard in Java 25
questions.explanation: JEP 512 finalised compact source files, instance main methods and java.lang.IO in Java 25.
